R7b is built. There is a new builder `scripts/race3d/builders/landmarks.gd` with its own shader `assets/shaders/modern/landmark.gdshader`. Every landmark Arcade shows now stands at Arcade's anchor on the path, out to 1,900 m. It uses Arcade's law (`RoadRenderer.landmark_fade`, unit test deviation < 1e-5) and the night floodlight. Beyond 0.70 L it fades with a translucent variant instead of the dither (B-09); at full coverage that variant is pixel-identical to the opaque one (measured 0 of 921,600 px).

Representation follows one order, which is the AS6 interface: a manifest model first, then Arcade's picture, then Arcade's procedural kind built as a real 3D shape (domed church, TV tower, lighthouse with beams, skyscraper group; N2), then the fallback set. No instance uniforms (A-19).

`layers/backdrop.gd` now draws the destination skyline as Arcade does: sprite silhouettes, plus Arcade's own 2D drawings through a RoadRenderer that is never added to the tree. A silhouette fades out while its 3D landmark is in range. `props.gd` needed no change: the skip for landmarks was already there (lines 88, 122, 329, 539, 741).

result.look_verdict:
Measured on llvmpipe, pictures at Hoch.

Better than Arcade: the procedural landmarks are real 3D shapes. By day they read better than Arcade's flat drawings and much better than the old wide fallback card: the Belgrade church with green domes, the slim Dortmund TV tower with its basket, the Madrid glass towers with floor bands, and the Hannover town hall dome.

Equal to Arcade: pictures (Elbphilharmonie, Kaiserburg, Eiffel tower, Atomium, Koekelberg) sit at Arcade's place and look the same. At night they are floodlit or lit like Arcade, and the Hamburg and Paris clips show no jump or dither. The skyline sits on the panorama like Arcade's, with no doubling. Below the horizon the far ground reads as land at S1-S5 and the arrivals.

Worse than Arcade: the red aviation light of the TV tower is about 3x Arcade's dot, and the tower shaft is brighter at night. The Elbphilharmonie is a little brighter at night. In bends at about 260 m the domed shapes sit up to about 85 px (6-7 %) off Arcade's flat drawing: Leipzig is lower and further left, Belgrade wider and further right, because the shape turns with the road and the dome stands 25 m behind its front. The lighthouse beams were hardly visible in the one frame taken.

Missing: real landmark models (AS6). The 600-m arrival views mostly do not show the landmark at all, because houses hide it in both modes, so near views were added.

It is the envelope of all sight lines of length L along the actual path, with the camera on every row in every lane; L = min(300 m, F2 need/0.6 + 9 m). The code is scripts/race3d/sight_corridor.gd, computed once per stage and precomputed by the streamer. Terrain, props, city fences and border pillars all read this one envelope. result.verdict: R7b is solid. Nothing in it is broken, and it can go into RINT-M3 after two small night-look fixes (B-01, B-02). I measured every gate myself on 2c154bc. Arcade golden check: 20/20 and 17/17 identical. A full run_tests passed (945 s). modern_sight and modern_path_check --full both passed. 6 of 6 selected render checks passed, and the stage result matches the base. A data scan of all 143 landmarks in 128 stage directions found no difference from Arcade in representation, set, scale or tint, and every landmark builds headless. The new tests guard their rules: 16 of 18 mutations were caught. The two that slipped through are the floodlight on plain props (B-03). File ownership was kept, apart from one foreign test file that R7b reported itself. The look was judged against Arcade and the base on the same simulation state. By day, the 3D shapes are clearly better than the base, which drew wide stand-in blocks at Dortmund, Madrid, Calais, Hannover and Belgrade. Hannover and Dortmund also look better than Arcade's flat drawings. Sprite landmarks look the same as Arcade. Worse than Arcade: at night the Elbphilharmonie is about 28 % brighter than both Arcade and the base. The aviation light is about 23 times Arcade's dot area, not the 3 times the R7b report claims. Close up, the domed shapes sit lower or to the side: Leipzig's dome is hidden behind a tree, and Belgrade's is about 85 px off. The unmirrored church on the left side stands up to 37.8 m closer to the road than in Arcade. At most 600-m city arrivals, houses hide the landmark in all three modes, so those views cannot show a difference.
